Child's echo read and parent's command read share the same stdin (fd 0) due to fork. Timing: parent reads command first, then child's echo reads remaining stdin. This creates a race/coordination point.

uncertainties.description: Whether child's canary can be leaked or bypassed to achieve RIP control in child process
uncertainties.reason: Canary is present and checked. No obvious leak path in child (seccomp restricts output to write(1) only, but child writes to pipe not stdout). Need S2 to analyze if canary can be recovered.

uncertainties.description: Exact value of sent_bytes that parent will receive after child echo overflow
uncertainties.reason: strlen(output_buf) depends on where first null byte is in the overflowed buffer. If overflow payload contains no nulls, strlen could return very large value. Need S2/dynamic analysis to confirm.

uncertainties.description: Whether parent's canary can be bypassed when parent stack is overflowed via sent_bytes
uncertainties.reason: Parent also has canary check. If parent overflow reaches canary, it will trigger __stack_chk_fail. Need S2 to determine if canary can be leaked or if overflow can avoid canary region.

uncertainties.description: Whether the movsxd sign-extension of sent_bytes in parent can be exploited (negative values)
uncertainties.reason: sent_bytes is read as int then movsxd to rdx for read size. If sent_bytes is negative, rdx would be very large (0xffffffff????????). read() with huge size may return less than requested, but the buffer overflow still occurs. Need S2 analysis.

uncertainties.description: Whether child process can perform useful ROP despite seccomp (mmap+mprotect available for shellcode, or open+read+write via ROP if allowed)
uncertainties.reason: Seccomp allows mmap(9) and mprotect(10), which could enable shellcode execution. But no open/read/write to arbitrary files except fd 0/1. Need S2 to assess ROP feasibility under seccomp.

uncertainties.description: Whether the parent's read(pipe2_rd, output_buf, sent_bytes) can overflow enough to control parent RIP without hitting canary first
uncertainties.reason: output_buf at rbp-0x110, canary at rbp-0x8. Overflow must pass canary to reach ret. Unless canary is known/leaked. Need S2 to analyze canary leak paths.
